title: Netherlands: a long power or water outage
short: What to expect over three days without power, and the government's pages for power cuts and no tap water
intro: A three-day power-outage example from the Dutch government's booklet, with the steps it says to take beforehand, plus the government's pages for a power cut and for no water from the tap. Shown only in a library that holds the Netherlands documents.

choices.label: The power is out and may stay out
choices.hint: The first hours: who to call, what to switch off, keeping warm

read.label: No power: what to do during a power cut
read.note: Do not call 112; the national power failure number is 0800-9009. Listen to regional radio, unplug sockets, keep warm in the smallest rooms, check on people who need help.

read.label: Timeline: the first hours of a grid power outage
read.note: From the start to +8 hours: what stops working, when 112 gets hard to reach, when phone signal fails and when an NL-Alert arrives.

read.label: Day 1 example: light, warmth, a radio, non-perishable food
read.note: A made-up evening without power and the steps it says to take beforehand for light and warmth, news and food.

choices.label: There is no water from the tap
choices.hint: Check the main tap, ask neighbours, emergency water after 24 hours

read.label: Drinking water: no water from the tap
read.note: Check the main tap and ask neighbours; after 24 hours without water, water companies supply emergency water from tanks; a boil notice comes by NL-Alert.

read.label: Day 2 example: no running water, low phone battery
read.note: The impact spreads on day 2; steps to take beforehand include 3 litres of water per person per day for 72 hours, stored cool and dark.

choices.label: It has been days: what comes next?

read.label: Timeline: from +8 hours to +72 hours
read.note: Traffic and petrol pumps, water and food at 24 hours, batteries at 36, neighbours and the radio at 48, government information at 72.

read.label: Day 3 example: help from neighbours and an agreed plan
read.note: A central place in the neighbourhood has information and help; steps to take beforehand for contact with others.

read.label: Emergency support offices run by the municipality
read.note: Where municipalities are setting up local offices for information and urgent help if an emergency lasts a long time.

choices.label: My phone is dying and I need reliable news
choices.hint: Power bank, one phone on, regional radio

read.label: Steps for a low phone battery and for reliable information
read.note: Keep a full power bank, set screen brightness low and close apps, keep one phone on for NL-Alerts, and use only reliable sources.

read.label: Use a battery radio for the regional broadcaster
read.note: The regional public broadcaster can keep broadcasting when the power and internet are down; the frequency list is on the next page.

read.label: FM frequencies by region
read.note: Transmitter locations and MHz for the regional radio stations.

limits.text: A power cut is not an acute emergency: do not call 112 for it. The national power failure number is 0800-9009.
In a long power outage 112 and the emergency services can be hard to reach because many people are asking for help.
If tap water does not meet quality standards, an NL-Alert will advise boiling it for 3 minutes first.
If you have run out of food, drink or medicines in a long emergency, an emergency support office can tell you what to do.

prepare.label: The kit list: water, food, light, warmth, radio, cash
prepare.note: At least 3 litres of water per person per day, non-perishable food, candles and matches, blankets, a battery radio, a charged power bank and cash.

prepare.label: Water to store, and a clean bucket or bottles for emergency water
prepare.note: Bottled water for at least 72 hours, 3 litres per person per day, plus a bucket, empty bottles or a jerry can for collecting emergency water.

prepare.label: Think ahead: what in your home depends on electricity
prepare.note: Check what depends on power, think through a long cut, and put together a kit with water, food, a torch, a radio and a power bank.

learn.label: Prepare for an emergency situation (the whole booklet, text-only edition)
learn.note: The 32-page booklet in English, with the three-day power-outage example on pages 20 to 23.
